panels.description: When the shown run started and its verdict: Issues found = a link lost or replaced the key; OK = no link did; No report = the run folder has no report.json (crashed or still running). Whole run, not filtered.
Distinct pages opened with the selected devices. Not split by route: every page is checked for all routes.
Page visits with the selected devices (one visit = page + profile, all scenarios). Not split by route.
Links whose destination was followed and compared with the referral key. From coverage in report.json, which has no breakdown by device or route, so the Profile and Route filters do not change it.
Links that kept the referral key. From coverage in report.json, which has no breakdown by device or route, so the Profile and Route filters do not change it.

Links that lost the referral key or carry another value in its place (coverage.checks.mismatch). From coverage in report.json, which has no breakdown by device or route, so the Profile and Route filters do not change it.

properties.value: Key lost or replaced · whole run

panels.description: untested[] entries of the selected devices, e.g. a QR code hidden on this screen or a click that led nowhere. untested[] entries have no route, so the Route filter does not apply here; the Profile filter does.
run.startedAt to run.finishedAt of report.json. Whole run.

Per device: distinct start pages (sitemap + start list) the run opened, of coverage.pages.start. Opened = a visit whose path is only the enter step. When coverage.scenarios.entry (start-page visits, all devices) reaches start x devices, every device opened all. Otherwise counted from pages[], which keeps only visits with problems or not-checked items; if that misses some start-page visits the number is a lower bound, shown as ≥.
panels.title: Start pages opened · of sitemap total

panels.description: Stopped early (limit) = some device did not open every start page. The walker takes one-step paths first, so an unopened start page means the run was cut (time limit, or a start visit given up). Start pages all opened = every device opened every start page; it cannot tell whether deeper clicks were cut. Whole run.

coverage.scenarios of report.json: visits per scenario. A visit counts for every scenario its path belongs to, so a start-page visit counts for all four; in short runs that only open start pages all four are equal. Whole run, not filtered.
panels.title: Visits by scenario · whole run

panels.description: Last 14 days (UTC), not filtered, from the metrics every run pushes (Prometheus), so runs that left no report count too. Each day shows the status of the run that ended last that day, over all processes. OK = no link lost the key; Issues found = at least one link lost or replaced the key; No report = the run ended without report.json, or its process went away (crash, PC off) before the run ended; Missed = no run started that day. An empty cell = the only run of the day is still going. Days before the metrics existed (2026-09-27) show Missed.

panels.description: One row per page for the selected devices and routes (pages[] of report.json summed over its visits; one visit = page + profile). The arrow lists the page's problems; the same problem (href, selector, actual, route, checked, expected) seen on several of the selected devices is one row; path is from its first occurrence. actual null = no key found; a single empty row with route "no problems" = the page had no key problems (only Not checked ones). Not checked ignores the Route filter (untested items have no route). Long cells are one line: hover a cell and click its inspect icon.
